title: Account deletion with a grace period
description: Self-service and admin account deletion for server apps: re-authenticated requests, a configurable grace period during which the account is disabled, cancel to restore access, session revocation through a hook, a declared delete/anonymize/retain data policy run by a leased, resumable, run-once worker, a PostgreSQL store and a Fetch adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build and Web Crypto (randomUUID), TextDecoder and the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core; mount the HTTP adapter under one prefix and call runDue() from your scheduler or job queue.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlAccountDeletionStore with your query executor; on other databases implement AccountDeletionStore with one live (pending, executing or completed) request per user and conditional, lease-checked claim, renew, step, complete and release statements.
Implement authorize(actor, 'request'|'cancel'|'read', {userId, self}) so owners (self) and the admins you choose are allowed.
Pass revokeSessions(userId) that revokes every session, refresh token and API token of the user.
Declare the data policy: one entry per data set with action delete, anonymize or retain, a reason, and an idempotent run(); put the account row itself last.
Set graceMs (default 30 days) and recentAuthMs (default 5 minutes); give actors authenticatedAt from your sign-in or re-authentication step.
Call isDisabled(userId) in sign-in and request authentication; for a disabled account offer only the cancel flow after verifying credentials.
Call runDue({limit}) periodically from a scheduler or the durable-jobs module; set leaseMs longer than one policy step takes.
Mount createAccountDeletionHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins and your authenticate(request).
limitations: Does not delete data, revoke sessions, verify passwords or store users itself; the application injects authorize, revokeSessions and the policy handlers.
Policy handlers must be idempotent: a crash after a handler finished but before its step was recorded runs that handler again on the retry.

A worker that keeps running after its lease expired is fenced: it renews its lease before each request and each handler and stops when renewal fails, but a handler call already in progress when the lease expires is not stopped. Set leaseMs well above the longest step.
Failed steps retry after retryDelayMs without a maximum; attempts and lastError are recorded for alerting, but there is no dead-letter state.
Request inserts the pending row before calling revokeSessions; if revocation throws, the row is discarded and revoke-failed is raised, but sessions revoked before the failure stay revoked.
isDisabled is a gate the application must call on sign-in and on authenticated requests; the module cannot block access paths it is not called from.
Deletion in backups, logs, search indexes, analytics and third-party processors is outside the module; declare and implement it as policy handlers or document it.

The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only. The SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which is a single connection: the concurrent runDue test proves the single conditional claim UPDATE gives each due account to one worker when statements interleave, not behavior under real multi-connection contention or on every hosted Postgres.
Legal retention periods, erasure obligations and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: routes: GET|POST|DELETE {prefix}/{userId|me}; POST schedules → 202, DELETE cancels during the grace period
30-day default grace; request/cancel need sign-in within 5 min, else 401 reauth-required
deletion runs from runDue() in your scheduler, not an HTTP route; needs a deletion store

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/account-deletion.test.mjs tests/account-deletion-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: request requires authenticatedAt within recentAuthMs (missing, stale and future times are refused with reauth-required)
a request is scheduled graceMs later (including 0) and nothing runs before scheduledFor
isDisabled is true while pending or executing and after completion, false after cancel
cancel during the grace period restores access; after the period ends or once executing it fails with too-late
revokeSessions is called on request; when it throws, the request is discarded, nothing is scheduled and revoke-failed is raised
the policy runs in order: delete and anonymize handlers change the application data, retain entries keep it and are recorded as steps
the policy is validated: at least one entry, unique names, delete|anonymize|retain, a reason, and run() for delete and anonymize
only the owner (self) or an authorized admin can request, cancel or read; admins also need recent authentication
one live request per user: already-pending while open, already-deleted after completion, including a request whose read raced completion (enforced by the store/unique index, not only the read)
a failed step is released with its error and retried after retryDelayMs, skipping steps already recorded
a crashed worker's lease expires, the next run resumes from the recorded steps and the stale worker cannot record steps or complete

each worker renews its lease before every request and handler; a queued request whose lease expired and was taken by another worker is reported lost and never touched again (memory store and PostgreSQL)
completion is recorded with completedAt and attempts; later runs do nothing
two concurrent runDue calls execute each due account exactly once on PostgreSQL (single conditional UPDATE with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) and on the memory store
HTTP adapter: GET status, POST request 202, DELETE cancel, 401, re-auth 401, 403 origin and authorization, 409, 413, invalid JSON, no-store and no claim token in responses
schema.sql applies and the SQL store passes the core behaviors on PostgreSQL

changes: First release: core, in-memory store, PostgreSQL schema and store, and Fetch adapter.
